observations.detail: The frozen domain patch validates occurredOn independently, preserves it on update unless explicitly changed, preserves plannedOn independently, clears effectiveOn for planned/suggested, records effectiveOn on pending-to-effective transition, and rejects explicit effectiveOn:null for posted/reconciled.

Domain tests use distinct occurred/planned/effective dates and assert planned->posted->reconciled transitions preserve economic and planned history while recording cash-effect dates; they also cover explicit null rejection.

The new statement test uses one transaction with occurredOn in June, plannedOn in July and effectiveOn in August and proves the operational statement selects August; sibling cases prove planned and legacy fallbacks.

The new category-evolution integration test persists one posted transaction with occurredOn in January, plannedOn in February and effectiveOn in March and expects the realized report amount only in January.

Existing import deterministic reconciliation changes status/reconciledAt metadata without rewriting occurredOn, plannedOn or effectiveOn; legacy payable transition remains documented as compatibility fallback rather than a new universal date source.

docs/TRANSACTION_DATES.md defines each field, date-only determinism, origin/flow matrix, transition rules, per-consumer precedence, legacy fallbacks and explicitly forbids a universal temporal COALESCE; docs/README.md indexes it and STATUS_MATRIX marks only this capability as Feito.

Repository search for the exact status claim found only docs/STATUS_MATRIX.md as the live status source; broader date-term search did not reveal another live documentation claim that the formalization remains pending.

Material candidate is exactly one commit ahead of base and changes ten files. The visual compatibility fixture now uses the canonical installment creation API to create a reconciled installment with an explicit historical effectiveOn, preserving the grouping-guard scenario without bypassing API ownership.

PR #624 is open and mergeable.
